subject: Autoscale SLO qualification / follow-up (FastPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@fastpay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fastpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - follow-up from demo

Hi John / Priya 

Thanks again for the demo time today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key SLO/scale behaviors we discussed and call out the follow-ups so we can land on a PoC config that matches FastPay's production needs.

Recap (from today's call):
- SLO targets we heard: p99 tail latency target for short inference (<=64 tokens) ~ 400ms; streaming-first-byte < 200ms; steady-state throughput target ~ 1.2k qps; expected concurrency ~ 500 concurrent active requests/streams.
- Workload characteristics you mentioned: mostly short prompts, heavy streaming (we estimated ~80% streaming), average tokens/request ~ 30-40.
- Burst behavior: expected brief peaks up to ~2.2k qps for 5-15 minutes during peak batch jobs and release events.
- Desired safety / fallback: low-latency fallback to smaller-capacity model for non-critical paths; queue maximums and graceful shedding preferred to long tails.

Autoscaling specifics we discussed and items for clarification:
- Warm pools: with a warm pool we can reduce cold-start scale-up time to under 30s for additional leaf capacity. Without warm nodes, cold scale-up to full reserved GPU capacity is in the ~3-6 minute range depending on model size.
- Scale-up policy: we recommend a hybrid policy - maintain a small warm pool sized for common bursts + autoscale additional pods; this keeps tail latency bounded while minimizing warm-nodes cost.
- Queueing: Redwood's serving runtime uses a short FIFO queue with priority for production-tier requests; we can configure max queue depth and max acceptable queue latency (we typically cap queue latency for SLOs at 100-200ms).

Action items / questions for FastPay so we can size PoC:
1) Can you share 24-72h traffic samples (qps over time), and a short breakdown by request type (streaming vs non-streaming)?
2) Typical sequence lengths (p50/p95 token counts) and percent of requests that are <64 tokens vs >256 tokens.
3) Which endpoints need strict p99 SLA vs best-effort?
4) Any constraints on warm pool cost or preferences for pre-warmed reserved capacity vs ephemeral scaling?

Attachments: I attached a short SLO summary and an initial pricing estimate for a Dedicated + warm-pool PoC.

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive / PoC scoping call (60 min) to align on exact PoC config and KPIs. Rishi, can you lead the technical call and propose a baseline PoC config?

Thanks 
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: slo_summary-fastpay.pdf, redwood_pricing.xlsx

From: John Lee <john.lee@fastpay.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - follow-up from demo

Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers to your questions below (happy to send samples via secure link):

- Traffic profile: baseline 600 qps, typical daytime peak windows reach 1.5k qps, occasional spikes up to 2.2k qps that last 5-10 minutes during batch reconciliation jobs.
- Streaming: ~85% of requests use streaming; first-byte latency is critical for UX.
- Sequence lengths: p50 ~ 28 tokens, p95 ~ 68 tokens. Very few requests go above 256 tokens (<2%).
- Endpoints: payment-authorize and fraud-check must have strict p99 SLA. Other auxiliary endpoints are best-effort.
- Concurrency: we currently see ~750 concurrent active sessions during peak.
- Warm pool cost: willing to budget for warm-pool if it materially reduces tail latency - please provide an estimate of incremental monthly cost for the PoC config.

Also attaching our internal requirements doc (I can share the full logs via the secure folder you suggested). We also have a brief security checklist - SOC2 plus network controls - which we'll share with your security team soon.

Thanks 
John Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
john.lee@fastpay.com

John / team 

Appreciate the traffic numbers   super helpful. Based on Marissa's recap and John's details, here's a proposed PoC baseline and next steps from a technical perspective:

Proposed PoC baseline (90-day):
- Dedicated setup: 2 reserved GPU pods for steady-state (sized to handle ~600 qps steady) + 4 warm pool nodes available for burst (warm nodes keep model kernels loaded and kv-cache warmed).
- Expected behavior: with the warm pool active, we expect to absorb spikes to ~2.2k qps within ~20-40s with p99 latency staying near target (~<450ms for short requests). Without warm pool, scale to full burst capacity would be ~3-6 minutes depending on model load.
- Queueing policy: short FIFO with high-priority lane for payment-authorize/fraud-check endpoints; set max queue latency threshold to 150ms for critical endpoints.
- Monitoring & SLAs: we will instrument per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, and drop rate; set alerts for p99 > 500ms and queue depth > 300.

Cost note: warm nodes increase monthly PoC cost - I'll ask Product to lock an estimate and share redwood_pricing.xlsx (attached by Marissa).

Next steps:
1) FastPay to share 72h traffic dump (anonymized: timestamps + qps + avg tokens) via the secure Drive link.
2) Schedule a 60-minute infra deep-dive week of Dec 6 - propose Tue Dec 8 10:00 PT (please confirm).
3) I'll work with Platform to size GPU types once we have the token distribution; incorporate a fall-back model variant for non-critical endpoints to reduce cost during sustained high load.

If the above looks good I'll draft a short mutual action plan (deliverables + timelines) and a PoC statement of work.

Thanks 
Rishi
